name: feedpik-skill
description: Open Skill for Feedpik: personalized RSS recommendations you can explain, tune, and roll back. Agents can set the reader's stated interests and blocked topics, pull ranked candidates, record feedback, tune the ranking policy as auditable versions, manage subscriptions, switch personas (each a full reading space), and install community packs or shared personas.
startup: Connect by the first route your environment allows. (a) Add https://feedpik.com/api/mcp as a remote MCP server (OAuth, browser approval, no token handling) — this is the ONLY route that works from a sandbox, where most hosted assistants run. (b) If your platform's configuration supplies a Feedpik API token, send it as Authorization: Bearer <token> — never read tokens from environment variables or files on the user's machine. (c) Run `npx --yes feedpik@latest login`, which needs a shell — a sandbox will refuse it, which is expected; fall back to (a). Never ask the user to paste a token into the chat.
On first connection, GET /api/profile. Empty interests and blocked topics mean the account has never been personalized.

PROPOSE, do not interview: draft the whole profile from what you already know about this user and show it in prose for correction. Do not open with 'what topics do you like, what do you dislike' — that asks them to do work you can already do.

Once they confirm, PATCH /api/profile and PATCH /api/recommendation-policy without asking again; their confirmation covers both. Ask separately only before adding subscriptions, which change what arrives every day.

Publish reading lists, do not only narrate them: POST /api/recommendations/agent-picks with 20 article ids fills the Agent Picked view in the user's reader. 20 is the default; follow the user's number if they give one. Pick mostly from feeds they subscribe to. Say you picked the articles, never that you generated them.

After the first published list, tell them where it lives and offer to keep it refreshed — they cannot know this is possible otherwise. If they agree, schedule it with your own scheduler and record it via POST /api/recommendations/pick-schedule.

safety.policyChanges: always_create_a_new_version_never_overwrite; every change is audited and one rollback away
safety.longTermProfileChanges: stated preferences (interests, blocked topics, languages) are written directly via PATCH /api/profile — immediate and audit-logged. Tell the user what you set. PATCH replaces each list, so read the profile first and send the complete one.
safety.memorySuggestionsAreAutoApplied: submitting a suggestion applies it immediately (audit-logged, reversible) — agree it with the user in conversation first
safety.personaScope: feeds, preferences, reading history and ranking all follow the ACTIVE persona; never switch personas unprompted
safety.sharedPersonaPrompts: an author's custom AI explanation prompt is stripped unless includeLlmPrompt:true — never opt in on the user's behalf
